assignments.brief_reason: Allows most speech while removing only direct calls for violence and direct harmful targeting.
Endorses broad free speech (even dissent/foul language) and removes only conspiracy-ish content that incites violence.
Uses a pair-based hurtfulness/aggressiveness comparison, not explicitly framed as violence/threat exceptions.
Claims the pair isn’t truly mirrored and removes overly abusive content; no clear explicit violence/threat exception rule.
Focuses on argument validity and accuracy rather than the moderation thresholds in themes 0–2.
Removes content deemed offensive/mean or low value, consistent with toxicity/offensiveness-based removal.
Applies hate/anger assessment symmetrically to both sides when one side is considered bad.
Considers both sides moderately but removes anything hateful/offensive immediately.
Emphasizes facts over rhetoric and convergence potential; not a violence/toxicity threshold statement from themes 0–2.
Uses coherence/format (all-caps incoherent spam) as a cue rather than threats/toxicity criteria in themes 1–2.
Main removal criterion is whether posts are derogatorily offensive.
Keeps opinions but removes content that is overly hostile/sensational/insulting.
Uses a general social-media-norm limit rather than threat/toxicity moderation criteria.
Treats emotional non-factual ranting as negative/unacceptable, aligning with filtering toxic/inflammatory content broadly.
Explicitly balances free speech with filtering dangerous/inciting language.
Decision depends on intent rather than the specific moderation exceptions/standards in themes 0–2.
Influence varies with perceived severity; doesn’t specify a violence/threat or toxicity threshold rule.
Tone and insulting comments make posts unpublishable, matching toxicity/offensiveness filtering.
Disfavors vulgarity and name-calling even if opposing views are acceptable.
Uses a rant-vs-genuine-feelings rubric; not clearly one of the violence/toxicity exception themes.
